The *Adhigayhamanasikārakathā* (Kv 16.4) is a debate text included in the sixteenth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, situated within the Abhidhamma Piṭaka of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. One translation in a modern language is cataloged by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
While no standalone parallels in other early Buddhist canons are registered, SuttaCentral records numerous cross-references and shared citations across canonical and paracanonical literature [SuttaCentral]. In Pali sources, these include the *Uppādāsutta* (AN 3.136), verses from the *Dhammapada* (Dhp 277, 278, 279), the *Theragāthā* (Thag 15.1), sections of the *Mahāniddesa* (Mnd 4) and *Cullaniddesa* (Cnd 6, 12, 16), as well as passages in the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 4, 37) and *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 2) [SuttaCentral]. Related verses and thematic parallels in other languages noted by SuttaCentral include the Gāndhārī *Dharmapada* (*G-Dhp* 97–134), the Patna *Dharmapada* (*P-Dhp* 358–375), the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 12, UVS 12), and Chinese versions in T 210, T 212, and T 213 [SuttaCentral].
Pali-internal text-reuse analyses conducted by DharmaNexus indicate that the text shares 1,243 matching passages across 50 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. This reuse consists predominantly of recurring Abhidhamma dialectical sequences shared with other chapters of the *Kathāvatthu*, most heavily with the *Sabbamatthītikathā* (Kv 1.6), the *Atītakkhandhādikathā* (Kv 1.7), the *Ariyantikathā* (Kv 3.2), the *Rūpaṁkammantikathā* (Kv 8.9), and the *Nirodhakathā* (Kv 10.1) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus reports no cross-language matches meeting its threshold score [DharmaNexus].
